text:
marta: Heads-up: we had a burst of ECC/Xid alerts from us-west GPU nodes last night — ~25 alerts over ~2h. PagerDuty fired a few pages and oncall had to triage repeatedly. I looked at dcgm-exporter logs; these are short spikes that clear within a couple minutes

sam: Saw it. The current Prometheus rule is too sensitive: it fires on any `dcgm_gpu_ecc_count_total` delta > 0 within 5m. That catches transient noise. We should gate on a sustained increase and coalesce per-card so we don't create N alerts for the same physical GPU.

liam: +1. Also worth adding hysteresis so a single blip doesn't trigger drain workflows. We want to differentiate "noisy card" vs "bad card".

jess: Can someone propose a minimal rule change we can A/B in staging? I can roll and watch for false negatives.

marta: Proposal (draft rule to test):
```
- alert: GpuEccPersistent
  expr: increase(dcgm_gpu_ecc_count_total[10m]) > 3
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    runbook: https://redwood.internal/infra/gpu-ecc-triage
```
This aims to ignore single blips and only fire when a card accumulates several ECC events in a sliding 10m window.

sam: Minor tweak: use `>= 3` and create a recording rule first to dedupe/group: `gpu_ecc_10m = increase(dcgm_gpu_ecc_count_total[10m])` and then alert on `gpu_ecc_10m{gpu_index!=""} >= 3` `by (instance,gpu_index)`. That avoids cross-series duplicates and makes suppression easier.

liam: Also add a soft-suppression label for known noisy cards (we keep a small list) so ops isn't flooded. If `gpu_ecc_10m >= 3` and `node_label ~ noisy=true` then route to lower-priority channel.

infra-bot: ACTION: prometheus/rules patch queued for staging at 2024-05-12T03:00Z. Notifying @jess for rollout.

jess: I'll roll to staging tonight and create a temp dashboard (gpu_ecc_10m, dcgm logs, node annotations). Will monitor for 12h and report back.

oncall-bot: Reminder: update oncall playbook - do NOT auto-drain on single alert. Only auto-drain when `gpu_ecc_24h > 100` OR manual triage confirms kernel oops.

marta: Operational note: when we do manual drains, use: `kubectl drain NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300` and tag node with `kubectl label node NODE gpu.faulty=true` so autoscaler and node-replacement tasks avoid immediate reprovisioning onto same hardware.

sam: After staging, backfill 7d of metrics to estimate how many alerts would have been suppressed. We should quantify impact (pages avoided vs missed real failures).

jess: Will post back with numbers. Also adding a small grafana panel that overlays old-rule vs new-rule alerts for quick comparison.

liam: One more suggestion: for nodes that show repeated short spikes, temporarily bump dcgm-exporter scrape interval to 10s (from 15s) on those nodes for better resolution while we triage. But watch scrape_targets growth.

marta: Agree. If staging looks good, we do 24h prod canary (roll to 10% of cluster) then full rollout. Meeting to sync tomorrow 09:30 PT if needed. Thanks all :thumbsup:
